messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — elevated error rates and OOM signals on inference-hosts in us-west-2, auto-paging Lina (oncall).
Lina (oncall): I’m looking. Context?
Sam: Seeing KV cache memory spike + lots of small speculative frames causing large continuous batches -> paging. CPU and GPU stalls too.
Mike-ML: Confirmed: speculative-decoding was enabled in last rollout (canary) and we hit a draft/target mismatch with KV entries; lots of duplicate KV keys being written, TTLs not respected.
Anya-SRE: On the infra side we’re seeing host swap activity and kernel reclaim spikes at 11:42 UTC. Pod restarts due to OOM killer on 3 nodes.
Lina (oncall): Impact? which customers?
Jamie-CS: Two mid-market customers reported latency spikes and 5xx errors for 10–30 minutes. One reported request timeouts in production.
Eli: Logs show continuous-batching batch sizes jumping from ~8 to >1024 for short tails, then fail because KV lookup latency skyrockets.
Sam: This looks like an interaction: speculative-decoding emits draft KV keys that differ from target KV shapes; the KV cache dedup logic was incorrectly merging draft keys causing cache blowups.
Mike-ML: Repro locally with a traffic replay: enable speculative decode + continuous batching + small seq lengths -> global key churn + rapid growth of cache index.
Lina (oncall): Short-term mitigation options?
Anya-SRE: We should immediate mitigate at infra: 1) disable speculative-decoding feature flag in prod config, 2) set max_batch_size to 64 for the affected pool, 3) force a KV-cache compaction and drop large indexes. Can do 1 and 2 now.
Sam: I can flip the flag and adjust autoscaler policy. Will push a config change to the hosted route group.
Lina (oncall): Go for it. Please notify if any deploys change model routing.
deploy-bot: Deploy started by Sam — config: speculative_decode=false, max_batch_size=64 for pool inference-prod-usw2.
Eli: Also an idea: temporarily turn off prefix/KV caching for requests with speculative header until we patch dedup logic. That prevents stale draft entries from polluting cache.
Mike-ML: Good call. We'll revert caching for the speculative path. I’ve got a hotfix branch that changes key namespace to include draft/target tag; but we need testing before rollout.
Sam: Config deploy finished. Observability shows batch sizes falling back to 8–64 and memory pressure decreasing. CPU contention down.
Anya-SRE: Started a manual KV compaction on the affected shard set — reclaiming ~45GB of index. Will continue background compaction.
Jamie-CS: Both customers report latency improving after the change, one says errors stopped ~3 minutes after deploy. :relieved:
Lina (oncall): Nice. Can we add a guardrail so future speculative runs can't create index thrash?
Mike-ML: Short-term: add a circuit-breaker that rejects speculative results when KV insert rate > threshold; long-term: patch dedup to namespace keys correctly and ensure draft/target sync atomicity.
Eli: Also adding a rate limiter to continuous batching: limit batch growth per-request-path and prefer splitting awkward small-seq traffic to the non-batched path.
Lina (oncall): Handing off to Anya for SRE follow-through and postmortem. I’ll be offline in 20m.
Anya-SRE: Taking over. Current action list: 1) Verify compaction completed, 2) run full index integrity checks, 3) add alert for KV insert rate anomaly, 4) coordinate with Mike for a safe patch release.
Anya-SRE: Assigning owners: Mike -> fix key namespace + unit tests, Eli -> batching guardrails + e2e replay, Sam -> rollback plan and config gating, Jamie -> customer comms update.
Mike-ML: ETA for patch: 6–8 hours dev + 2–3 hours staged rollout. I’ll open PR and link tests.
Sam: Will prepare a canary route with feature-flag gating so we can validate before wider rollouts.
Eli: I kicked off a traffic replay on staging with the exact sequence distribution; confirmed patch prevents duplicate key churn locally.
Anya-SRE: Risk notes for postmortem: - mutation of KV keyspace by speculative path not isolated - lack of throttling for continuous batching under churn - cache eviction policy didn’t account for heavy transient key insertion
Jamie-CS: CS note: customers want a concise timeline + mitigation summary. I’ll draft a message once we have the postmortem draft.
Lina (oncall): Thanks team. If anything regresses, re-ping with severity escalate.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed by Sam — speculative_decode flag disabled across inference-prod-usw2.
Anya-SRE: KV compaction finished at 11:58 UTC. Reclaimed ~52GB. Index integrity check in progress.
Eli: Metrics are stable for 20m: tail latency back to baseline, 5xxs reduced to pre-incident levels.
Mike-ML: Created PR #4223 with key-namespace fix and added a test that simulates draft->target transition.
Anya-SRE: Logging follow-ups: add structured tagging for draft vs target keys, add per-route KV insert meter, and create a dashboard for cache churn.
Lina (oncall): Last check before handoff complete: any blockers?
Sam: No blockers. Will coordinate staged rollout tomorrow.
Jamie-CS: I’ll send customer update summarizing: cause = interaction between speculative decoding + continuous batching causing KV index blowup; mitigation = disabled speculative flag, reduced max batch size, forced compaction; next = patch + staged rollout + postmortem.
Anya-SRE: Handoff to oncall rotation tomorrow: Eli will be primary for verification during rollout, Sam secondary.
Eli: Got it. I’ll watch the canary metrics and have rollback plan ready.
Anya-SRE: Postmortem owner: Mike-ML. Target draft in 48h.
Lina (oncall): Closing my oncall handoff notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
